newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait index sets new record but volume drops.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait index sets new record but volume drops.

text.p: Kuwait share index ended the week to Wednesday at a record high for the second time in as many weeks but volume and value dropped.
The index rose two percent to 1,782.2 points from last week's 1,747 record and 6.6 percent from a month ago.
In recent weeks trading volume and value set records but dealers said they corrected this week after large capital flows to the market fueled already active trade.
Value fell 24.3 percent to 224.3 million dinars ($750 million), a daily average of 44.9 million dinars. Volume dropped 29.6 percent to 1.06 billion shares, a daily average of 212 million.
"But share prices are still going high. A (overall) correction could occure soon," one dealer predicted.
Gainers led loosers 30-10 this week while 14 were unchanged.

Commercial Bank, Bahrain International Bank, United Realty Co, Coast Investment and Development Co, Kuwait Investment Projects Co, Pearl of Kuwait Real Estate Co and Kuwait Real Estate Co were among the most traded shares.

Property firms were the most active sector by value with 30 percent, investment shares followed with 28 percent and banks with 19.8 percent. Investment firms were the most active by volume with 32 percent.

Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Kuwait's foreign residents can invest through mutual funds ran by Kuwaiti firms.
